It is a scene of the open sky. A massive bird, its wings outstretched, takes up the center of the mosaic. In its beak it holds a twisting knot made of sun-bleached rowan wood. The image of the bird on the true cathedral's ceiling would likely be white if it was still intact, but here it is black. Its feathers look almost like scales in the flickering torchlight, and for just a moment, the image of the bird is replaced by a sight of a terrifying black scaled dragon, its yellowed talons reaching for the unwary adventurer.

The area is illuminated.

In this room you see: Bjeorn the Galirrim,  Raabilis the Galirrim
Obvious exits are: west, southwest, south, blackened doorway

[Twisted Cathedral Altar]
In a perverted twist on the altar in the true cathedral above, a massive white-veined black marble altar dominates the space. A thick dark liquid runs in a constant cascade in a fountain on the top of the altar, and a thick reddish mist hovers over the liquid in the bottom basin. The coppery scent of blood permeates the area, suggesting that the liquid in the fountain is the heart blood of dozens of daily sacrifices.

The area is illuminated.

[Twisted Cathedral East Wing]
The floor arches downward toward the center of the massive cathedral and the lining it tiles are scuffed and scraped, but it is more intact than the ceiling in the above room. It is a scene of the open sky. A massive bird, its wings outstretched, takes up the center of the mosaic. In its beak it holds a twisting knot made of sun-bleached rowan wood. The image of the bird on the true cathedral's ceiling would likely be white if it was still intact, but here it is black. Its feathers look almost like scales in the flickering torchlight, and for just a moment, the image of the bird is replaced by a sight of a terrifying black scaled dragon, its yellowed talons reaching for the unwary adventurer.

[Twisted Cathedral East Wing]
The floor arches downward toward the center of the massive cathedral and the lining it tiles are scuffed and scraped, but it is more intact than the ceiling in the above room. It is a scene of the open sky. A massive bird, its wings outstretched, takes up the center of the mosaic. In its beak it holds a twisting knot made of sun-bleached rowan wood. The image of the bird on the true cathedral's ceiling would likely be white if it was still intact, but here it is black. [Temple of the Eyranas]
Amazingly the interior of the temple is teaming with life. Birds fly freely amongst the tall trees and shrubs which give the appearance of the outside instead of in. Small animals scurry across the ground in an almost permanent state of play. A large fountain set in the center of the area spouts water high into the air which then settles back into the fountain without even the smallest splash. Statues of the Goddess's lie scattered among the various ponds and gardens of the temple. A small grassy pasture free of any growth takes its place on the northeastern side of the temple which sits beneath a beautiful green, moss covered altar. A gaggle of bushes trimmed to portray letters spells out the word "Life" in the northwestern corner of the temple. A small path that leads through some thick overgrowth to the west provides passage to another room. To the south an overgrown arch provides exit back to the street.

The area is illuminated.

l

[Temple of the Eyranas]
Amazingly the interior of the temple is teaming with life. Birds fly freely amongst the tall trees and shrubs which give the appearance of the outside instead of in. Small animals scurry across the ground in an almost permanent state of play. A large fountain set in the center of the area spouts water high into the air which then settles back into the fountain without even the smallest splash. Statues of the Goddess's lie scattered among the various ponds and gardens of the temple. A small grassy pasture free of any growth takes its place on the northeastern side of the temple which sits beneath a beautiful green, moss covered altar. A gaggle of bushes trimmed to portray letters spells out the word "Life" in the northwestern corner of the temple. A small path that leads through some thick overgrowth to the west provides passage to another room. To the south an overgrown arch provides exit back to the street.

The area is illuminated.

In this room are: moss-covered green marble altar
Obvious exits are: small path

[Temple of the Eyranas]
Amazingly the interior of the temple is teaming with life. Birds fly freely amongst the tall trees and shrubs which give the appearance of the outside instead of in. Small animals scurry across the ground in an almost permanent state of play. A large fountain set in the center of the area spouts water high into the air which then settles back into the fountain without even the smallest splash. Statues of the Goddess's lie scattered among the various ponds and gardens of the temple. A small grassy pasture free of any growth takes its place on the northeastern side of the temple which sits beneath a beautiful green, moss covered altar. A gaggle of bushes trimmed to portray letters spells out the word "Life" in the northwestern corner of the temple. A small path that leads through some thick overgrowth to the west provides passage to another room. To the south an overgrown arch provides exit back to the street.

The area is illuminated.

Amazingly the interior of the temple is teaming with life. Birds fly freely amongst the tall trees and shrubs which give the appearance of the outside instead of in. The small path ends as the trees part, revealing a small clearing. Sunlight filters down from above, splashing the vibrant green grass and wildflowers. The noise of the central part of the grove all but fades away in this quiet sanctuary. An altar of stone rests in the center of the small clearing of verdant grass. Tangled vines have grown wild across the hard stone and though no markings can be seen, it is obvious that this is a place sacred to the twin goddesses of nature. Overhead the soft warbling of songbirds blends with the chirping crickets below into a sublime symphony of sounds. Small trinkets of adoration and worship have been left at the base of the altar, each one a symbol of devotion to their beloved gods.

The area is illuminated.

[Burial Mounds, Path of Stone Might]

[Burial Mounds, Path of Stone Might]
Small bits of root have begun to break through the stone tunnel, now well underground. The way is lit by several pewter sconces holding tar-soaked torches. The light from the torches ignite a massive opal-like slab of stone that glitters with the names of the fallen Vorngar of the Alliance. The slab appears to have been opened, leaving the way to the burial mound unblocked.

The area is illuminated.

[Burial Mounds, Gnipaognhir]
Unlike more traditional burial mounds, the mound of the Vorngar is entirely cleft from stone. Stalagmites, stalactites, and calcite formations make up the whole of the cavernous mound, causing the area to resemble the many interconnecting holes of a porous stone.

The area is illuminated.

Obvious exits are: southwest, south, southeast, open opalescent slab

sw

[Burial Mounds, Gnipaognhir]

It appears that someone, or something, drilled holes into the stone walls of the cavern around a very large shape, the removal of which has caused a deep black gash in the wall. A stone cylinder of what resembles a skeletal finger lies discarded on the floor.

The area is illuminated.

Obvious exits are: south, southeast, east, northeast

e

[Burial Mounds, Gnipaognhir]

Shattered sprigs of the beard have fallen to the stone floor like mounds of ancient dust. The eerie eye holes of the face peer out, empty and shallow.

The area is illuminated.

Obvious exits are: west, southwest, south, southeast, east, north

e

[Burial Mounds, Gnipaognhir]
Black streaks mar the stone walls where a stalagmite has been severed from the stone floor. It looks as if it has been split in three pieces, possibly by claw marks. All around, the stone formations of the walls seem to resemble stocky faces, bodies, and limbs.

The area is illuminated.

Obvious exits are: northwest, west, southwest, south

[Burial Mounds, Gnipaognhir]
Several pitted jewels sparkle from the sides of the mound, paired together in sunken, porous holes. A few pickaxes line the walls where someone tried to dig out the jewels. A few appear to be missing where streaks of black smear the sides and floor of the stone mound.

The area is illuminated.

Obvious exits are: northwest, west, southwest, north

[Urda Town Square Center]
On this site, a fierce battle for control of the great city was waged, and on this site is where its citizens now celebrate that victory. Statues of the fallen heroes, and great leaders of the alliance adorn the tops of grand marble archways that scatter over the square. They stand ever vigilant against any unseen enemy. The people of Urda flock here to barter and trade, to converse with friends, or just relax near the fountain and have a game of chess. Benches and tables dot the landscape near the edge of the fountain. Hawkers of all type roll through this area with their wares, hoping to make a few coins. The many languages of races and guilds reverberate off the storefronts of the surrounding Merchant Square where a constant foot traffic ebbs and flows, making this the heart of the city.

The area is illuminated.

Statues of the fallen heroes, and great leaders of the alliance adorn the tops of grand marble archways that scatter over the square. They stand ever vigilant against any unseen enemy. [Travers Town Square]
Small marble benches are scattered neatly about the square welcoming travelers to take a seat or to possibly empty pebbles from their boots. Cobblestone streets decorate the square alternating from browns to reds in a random pattern. Small statues of the world's races stand behind each bench as if standing sentinel. Tall lamp posts with wrought iron lanterns look down on the neat and clean streets. An occasional waste engineer wanders through, sweeping up dirt and trash into tin dustpans. Tucked away in a corner is an old door leading to a rundown store. The loud echoing of dripping water can be heard coming from a metal grate which is recessed into the street.

The area is illuminated.
